intent: New material with no source to be faithful to. The absence of a source obligation raises the verification burden; it does not lower it.
may_change: everything — there is no source structure, wording, or framing to preserve
must_preserve: nothing from a source, because there is no source
internal consistency between claims made within the piece itself
the distinction between fact, interpretation, and hypothesis for every claim asserted (editorial/constitution.md §2)

new_claims.rationale: Every asserted fact carries the full verification burden precisely because there is no source to inherit fidelity from.

source_fidelity.rationale: There is no source-fidelity obligation at all; this value marks the absence of one rather than a degree of one.

structure_rule: Structure is chosen entirely by the argument the piece makes; there is no source topology to avoid mirroring because there is no source.
verification_burden: verify-claims treats every factual assertion as needing independent verification from scratch — original content gets no benefit of the doubt a source-derived transformation would.
anti_patterns: Asserting a fact with no verification because 'it's original, not sourced material'
Presenting a hypothesis or scenario with the confidence of a finding (editorial/constitution.md §2)
Borrowing the authority of an unstated source while claiming the piece is original
An empty uncertainty list — original work usually knows less than a synthesis of existing material, not more (editorial/constitution.md §3)
